title.value: Fault Development in Platform Limestones of the Maiella Thrust Sheet, Italy

note.value: The deformation mechanism associated with evolution of normal faults in Cretaceous platform interior carbonates of the Maiella thrust sheet, Itaiy is documented in this paper. The earliest structural features are bedding parallel stylolites that define mechanical layers. The bedding parallel stylolites were subjected to shearing probably in response to bending of the thrust sheet with top to the West motion, subparallel to the direction of transport. Shearing along bedding parallel stylolites results in stylolite clusters at a high angle to, and at the termination of, the sheared bedding parallel stylolites. The high angle sylolite clusters are consequently sheared in a normal sense whereby generating a third set of stylolites fragmenting the rock. With increasing slip magnitude, further fragmentation and weakening of the rock occurs within the adjacent mechanical packages. Linking of the fragmentation zone in adjacent mechanical packages to form a larger fault occurs along the weakest packages aligned in the direction of the normal faulting. At this stage the fragmented rock turns into breccia whose geometry and grain size varies from one mechanical bed to the next based primarily on the spacing of the bedding parallel stylolites or the thickness of the mechanical layers. Eventually polished and striated surfaces form at the edges of the breccia zones. Normal slip along clusters of stylolites accommodates extension typically provided by opening mode features such as veins or joints in other settings. In this study, the stages of normal faulting in a thrust belt setting have been documented from the incipient stage to just over 2 meters slip magnitude. A model showing stages of growth in the development of normal faults by hierarchical occurrence of pressure solution structures and their consecutive shearing is presented.
Graham, Brita. (2001). Fault Development in Platform Limestones of the Maiella Thrust Sheet, Italy. Stanford Digital Repository. Available at: http://purl.stanford.edu/wn200dn5426
